description: Blue-grey plates around a white star. Cold to hold, and nothing anyone has ever broken was carrying it.
lore: Grading is done by hand and mostly in the dark, because a grader who works by eye starts trusting colour, and colour is the least of what a stone is. The hands learn heft and warmth and the width of a seam. One tray to a kind of creature, and [[lore/the_hard_pieces|the rule underneath that]] has never yet failed.

This one is cold. Not cool — cold, the way a pebble out of a beck is cold, and it stays that way in a shut hand, so the hand has it before the eye has done anything at all. Blue-grey plates, a white star sunk in the middle, ninety gold. In a haft it bites frost, hardest at whatever is cold already.

The grader on the north bench keeps a tray with nothing else in it. She has been told to file them in with the crystal country's stones — same weight, same setting, same buyers — and she will not, and her reason is not an argument: those came off something, she has held them, this is not one of those. Her trays are named for creatures. That one has no name over it, and she keeps it standing so that if a name ever turns up she will know which stones to move. Six in it, over nineteen years. The other benches call that superstition and file theirs under frost with the rest — and every grader on every one of those benches can pick the odd stone out of a frost tray by touch, in the dark, first try.
gm_notes: Unbound, and left unbound: no creature is invented, asserted or implied beyond one grader's refusal to file it. The trays are the prop — a working grading floor other item records can reuse. Her sentence is deliberately not evidence; the last line is, and it is left where it lies. The shipped line said 'nothing anyone has killed' — replaced, nothing here is killed.
